Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As we scope our deployment plan, procurement has flagged the latency SLO language in the draft SOW. Two quick asks:

- Can you confirm whether Redwood reports p50/p95 as rolling percentiles (global across all frontends) or as fixed-window aggregates (e.g., 1m buckets)?
- We have an upcoming migration spike (end of Q3) and are concerned about a burst of slow tails while we finish warmups. Is there a documented path for a temporary SLO exemption or "transition period" so we don't trigger SLA remediation while we stabilize?

If you have a short note or template we can attach to the SOW that explains the measurement method and any limited carveouts, that would help procurement.

Appreciate it — would love a quick call if that's easier.

Hi Anita —

Thanks for the note and the thoughtful questions. Short answers up front:

- Measurement: by default our hosted API reports p50/p95 on per-request latencies aggregated into fixed, non-overlapping minute buckets for reporting and SLA calculation. We also maintain rolling-percentile diagnostics internally for troubleshooting.
- Temporary exemption: yes — we support a documented, timeboxed transitional carveout for migrations/big warmups. Typical pattern is a 30-day transition with a widened p95 window or a transient-carveout clause that excludes the largest X% of minutes from SLA calculations while the team stabilizes.

I've attached a draft proposal (redwood-p50p95-proposal-v2.pdf) and a worksheet that shows how different bucket windows change observed p95 (measurement-window-draft.xlsx). Soojin from Product Ops is cc'd and can provide the measurement-runbook.

If you like, we can join procurement + infra on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through.

Next steps I suggest: 1) agree carveout type (window widen vs transient minute drop), 2) document period and rollback criteria in SOW, 3) add simple monitoring alerts + a health-checked rollback.

Best,

Aditya/Soojin — quick internal note before we jump on the call with BlueCrest:

My recommendation: offer a 30-day transitional SLO with these guardrails:
- Expand the p95 measurement window from 1 minute to 5 minutes for the transition period (reduces sensitivity to temporary tail spikes).
- Exclude up to 2% of the highest-minute-latency minutes across the 30-day window from SLA calculations (transient-carveout).
- During the period, no SLA credits will be payable; instead we'll commit to a remediation playbook and weekly latency regression reports.

This preserves production incentives while giving customers breathing room. We should run the measurement-window-draft.xlsx against their traffic profile first so we can recommend the exact numbers.

Hi Anita —

Thanks for the follow-ups. A few clarifications and a concrete proposal:

Measurement scope
- We compute minute-level buckets at the regional serving edge (region = us/eu/apac) and publish both regional and global aggregates. For Hosted API SLAs we can bind the p50/p95 to regional aggregates if that is a commercial requirement.

Windowing approach (proposal)
- Baseline: p50/p95 computed on fixed, non-overlapping 1-minute buckets (standard product behavior).
- Transitional offer: 30-day timebox where p95 is computed over fixed 5-minute buckets for the affected region(s). This reduces noise from warmup tails.
- Optional transient carveout: allow exclusion of the top X% of minutes (we typically propose X=2%) if the customer supplies a staged warmup plan and key telemetry (cache pre-warm confirmation, replica warmup completion).

Operational commitments during transition
- No SLA credits during the transition, but Redwood will provide: weekly latency reports, daily warmup progress notes (first 10 days), and an automatic rollback trigger if p95 remains > 2x target for 72 continuous hours.
- We'll assign a Product Ops contact to run the measurement runbook and to share the worksheet (attached).

If that sounds acceptable we can put this into a short SOW addendum: measurement method, exact carveout percentage, start/end dates, rollback criteria, and reporting cadence. I've added a draft runbook here: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcDEF_redwood-bluecrest-measurement-runbook

Anita —

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Per the thread and the call, here is a short summary we can attach to the SOW:

1) Measurement: p50/p95 are computed from minute-level buckets at the regional edge. SLA calculations will be bound to the region specified in the SOW.

2) Transitional carveout (agreed path): 30-day timeboxed period for the initial migration to production. During this period we will compute p95 on fixed 5-minute buckets for the affected region(s).

3) Optional exclusion: BlueCrest may request up to a 2% highest-minute exclusion during the 30-day period if a staged warmup plan is provided and validated by Redwood Product Ops. Any deviation from 2% will require explicit approval.

4) Credits & remediation: no SLA credits are payable during the transition; Redwood will provide weekly latency reports, daily warmup updates for the first 10 days, and an automatic rollback trigger if p95 exceeds 2x target for 72 continuous hours.

5) Next steps: procurement to confirm the region(s) and start date; we'll draft a 1-page addendum for the SOW capturing the points above and circulate for signature. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/BC-9237

If that matches your understanding, please confirm and provide the procurement contact for DocuSign.

—Aditya
